text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed using specific blood tests administered and evaluated by a healthcare provider.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests administered and evaluated by a healthcare provider

list.snippet: A1C Test: Measures your average blood sugar level over the past 2 to 3 months. No fasting is required.
Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) Test: Measures your blood sugar after you fast (no food or drink except water) for at least 8 hours.
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): Measures your blood sugar 2 hours after you drink a special sugary liquid.
Random Plasma Glucose Test: Measures your blood sugar at any time of day, regardless of when you last ate.
Diabetes: 200 mg/dL or higher, typically accompanied by classic symptoms like increased thirst, frequent urination, or unexplained weight loss.
Repeat Testing: Unless you have clear symptoms and a high random blood sugar reading, doctors usually repeat the test on a second day to confirm the diagnosis.

Screening Guidelines: Major health organizations recommend routine screening for adults starting at age 35, or earlier if you have risk factors such as overweight or obesity, a family history of diabetes, or prediabetes.
Note: Over-the-counter blood glucose meters cannot be used to diagnose diabetes.

text_blocks.snippet: You can find more detailed guidance on testing criteria from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention or the American Diabetes Association.
